The Basics

What is plasma, exactly?

Plasma is the straw-colored liquid that makes up over half of your blood. It carries red and white blood cells and platelets throughout your body, and it's rich in proteins — antibodies, clotting factors, and albumin — that can't be manufactured synthetically.

Donated plasma is manufactured into therapies for people with bleeding disorders, primary immune deficiencies, burns, and trauma. Donating is simple: a machine draws your blood, separates the plasma, and safely returns your red cells and platelets to you.

Twice-weekly donation ~60–90 minute visit Life-saving therapies

Introduction To Plasma Donation

Six Steps, One Hour

The plasma donation process

Every visit follows the same careful sequence, from eligibility check to fluid replacement — designed for your safety and comfort at every stage.

01

Check eligibility

Confirm you meet age, weight, and health requirements before booking your first visit.

02

Make an appointment

Call ahead or simply walk in during our hours of operation — no long wait for a first slot.

03

Register

Complete a short form with your personal and medical history, and present valid ID, proof of address, and proof of Social Security.

04

Health screening

A medical professional checks your weight, blood pressure, and hemoglobin, and reviews your health history and medications.

05

Plasma collection

A needle draws blood that's separated into plasma by a specialized machine; your remaining blood components are returned to you. About 45–60 minutes.

06

Fluid replacement

Saline restores your fluid balance, and our team confirms your next eligible donation date before you head out.

After You Give

Post Donation Tips

Take care of yourself after donating plasma to feel your best and be ready for your next visit.

💧

Stay Hydrated

Drink at least 8–10 glasses of water over the next 24 hours. Avoid alcohol for at least 24 hours post-donation to help your body recover quickly.

🥗

Eat a Healthy Meal

Eat a nutritious meal rich in protein and iron within a few hours of donation. Good choices include lean meats, beans, leafy greens, and fortified cereals.

🛋️

Rest & Relax

Avoid strenuous exercise or heavy lifting for at least 24 hours. Take it easy and give your body time to replenish the donated plasma.

🩹

Care for the Donation Site

Keep the bandage on for at least 4–6 hours. If bruising or soreness occurs, apply a cold pack. Avoid submerging the arm in water for the rest of the day.

☕

Limit Caffeine

Reduce your caffeine intake for the rest of the day. Caffeine can act as a diuretic and may slow your body's rehydration process after plasma donation.

📅

Schedule Your Next Visit

You can donate plasma up to twice per week with at least 48 hours between donations. Plan ahead and book your next appointment to maximize your impact.

Why Should You Donate Plasma?

Plasma donation is one of the most impactful ways you can give back to your community. Your plasma contains proteins and antibodies that cannot be manufactured in a lab — they can only come from generous donors like you.

Life-Saving Medicine

Plasma-derived therapies treat over 80 rare and chronic conditions including hemophilia, primary immune deficiencies, and alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

Earn Real Compensation

Receive compensation via your Paysign debit card after every donation, with new donor bonuses that can add up to $500 in your first month.

🌐

Safe & Regulated

All collection follows strict FDA regulations. Your red blood cells and platelets are returned to you, and the needles used are always sterile and single-use.

About Us

Our Vision

A commitment to quality, safety, and community

Our vision at Care Plasma is to be the leading provider of high-quality plasma products while ensuring the safety and well-being of our donors and employees. We strive to make a positive impact on the lives of patients who depend on plasma-derived therapies to treat a wide range of medical conditions.

At our collection center, we are committed to maintaining the highest standards of quality and safety in all aspects of our operations. Our commitment to our donors is to provide a comfortable and safe environment for their donation experience.

We pledge to ensure that all plasma products collected are of the highest quality and meet or exceed all regulatory requirements. We are dedicated to continuous improvement in our processes and procedures, and to being responsible citizens who give back to the communities in which we operate.

Who Can Donate

Donor criteria

Age & weight

18 years or older, at least 110 lbs (50 kg), with a healthy hemoglobin level.

Travel

Recent travel to certain high-risk regions may result in a temporary deferral.

Medication

Some medications — certain antibiotics, blood thinners, immunosuppressants — may affect eligibility. Ask our staff about yours.

Lifestyle

Certain lifestyle factors or recent exposure to infectious disease may lead to deferral.

FAQs

Frequently Asked

Questions, answered

Please reach us at info@careplasma.com if you can't find an answer to your question.

What's the difference between donating plasma and donating blood?

Plasma donation collects only the liquid component of your blood and takes longer than whole-blood donation because the plasma is separated using a special machine — which is why donors are compensated for their time. Plasma can be donated up to twice in a 7-day period, while whole blood is limited to once every 56 days, since the body replenishes plasma faster than red blood cells.

How long does the process take?

Typically 60–90 minutes from check-in to completion, though timing can vary by visit and donor.

How often can I donate?

Most donors can give plasma up to twice per week, subject to our guidelines and your individual health status.

How much will I get paid?

Compensation varies with current promotions — new donors can earn up to $500 in their first month.

Does it hurt?

The needle insertion causes brief, mild discomfort, but the donation itself shouldn't be painful. Some donors experience mild dizziness or fatigue that typically resolves quickly.

Can I donate if I've received a COVID-19 vaccine?

Yes — most vaccinated donors are eligible, though waiting periods can vary by vaccine type and current policy. Our staff can confirm at check-in.

How is donated plasma used?

It's manufactured into medications for immune disorders and clotting factor deficiencies, and used in treating burns and trauma injuries, as well as in developing new therapies.

Available Jobs

Open roles at our New York City center

Physician Substitute (LPN/RN)

Under supervision of the Center Manager, Physician, and Quality Assurance Supervisor, and in compliance with Care Plasma's Standard Operating Procedures and State/Federal regulations, this role ensures donor suitability, donor safety, and product integrity.

Qualifications: EMT-P, LPN, or RN licensure in NY State (must be maintained); good oral and written communication skills; computer proficiency; CPR certified; able to stand/walk for a full shift; able to lift up to 5 lbs regularly, occasionally up to 32 lbs, and rarely up to 50 lbs.

Benefits: 401(k), health insurance, paid time off.

Phlebotomist

Responsible for the efficient and effective collection of plasma from donors — performing venipuncture, setting up the plasmapheresis machine, and monitoring the pheresis process in line with our Standard Operating Procedures.

Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent; phlebotomy certification and venipuncture experience preferred; strong communication with donors; able to set up, operate, and troubleshoot plasmapheresis equipment; standing/walking up to 100% of shift; occasional lifting up to 25 lbs.

Plasma Processor

Under supervision of the Center Manager and Quality Assurance Supervisor, this role processes, stores, packs, and ships plasma units and samples, and performs necessary equipment calibrations with thorough documentation.

Qualifications: High school diploma/equivalent; good oral and written communication; computer proficiency; able to stand/walk for a full shift; able to lift up to 50 lbs; able to work short periods in plasma freezers colder than -30°C.

Donor Screener

Under supervision of the Operations Supervisor and Quality Assurance Supervisor, this role determines donor suitability for plasmapheresis in compliance with our Standard Operating Procedures and State/Federal regulations.

Qualifications: High school diploma/equivalent; good oral and written communication; computer proficiency; able to stand/walk for a full shift; able to lift up to 5 lbs regularly, occasionally up to 32 lbs, and rarely up to 50 lbs.
